Guidance for AI coding agents working with this repository.

Fizzy is a kanban-style project management and issue tracker: cards move across columns on boards, with comments, mentions, and assignments.

## Deploy

Default branch: `main`

Self-hosted deploys run Kamal against `config/deploy.yml` — see `docs/kamal-deployment.md`.

## SaaS mode

For local agent work, `tmp/saas.txt` is the checkout-level SaaS switch used by `bin/setup`. When present, read `saas/AGENTS.md` before continuing. Otherwise, do not apply its instructions.

## Architecture Overview

### Multi-Tenancy (URL-Based)

Fizzy uses **URL path-based multi-tenancy**:
- Accounts have a unique decimal `external_account_id` used in URL prefixes
- URLs are prefixed: `/{account_id}/boards/...`
- Middleware (`AccountSlug::Extractor`) extracts the account ID from the URL and sets `Current.account`
- The slug is moved from `PATH_INFO` to `SCRIPT_NAME`, making Rails think it's "mounted" at that path
- Tenant-scoped domain records are account-isolated; global identity, session, and authentication records are exceptions
- Background jobs automatically serialize and restore account context

**Key insight**: This architecture allows multi-tenancy without subdomains or separate databases, making local development and testing simpler.

### Authentication & Authorization

Passwordless magic link authentication. A global `Identity` (email-based) can have `Users` in multiple Accounts, so an email is not a single account membership. Users have roles: owner, admin, member, system. Board-level access control via `Access` records.

### Entropy System

Cards automatically "postpone" (move to "not now") after inactivity:
- Account-level default entropy period
- Board-level entropy override
- Prevents endless todo lists from accumulating
- Configurable via Account/Board settings

### UUID Primary Keys

All tables use UUIDs (UUIDv7 format, base36-encoded as 25-char strings):
- Custom fixture UUID generation maintains deterministic ordering for tests
- Fixtures are always "older" than runtime records
- `.first`/`.last` work correctly in tests

### Background Jobs (Solid Queue)

Database-backed job queue (no Redis):
- Custom `FizzyActiveJobExtensions` prepended to ActiveJob
- Jobs automatically capture/restore `Current.account`
- Mission Control::Jobs for monitoring

Recurring tasks are declared in `config/recurring.yml`.

### Sharded Full-Text Search

Full-text search runs in the database, not Elasticsearch. On MySQL it is sharded 16 ways by CRC32 of the account ID (`Search::Record::Trilogy`); on SQLite it is a single FTS5 index (`Search::Record::SQLite`). Don't assume the sharded shape when working under SQLite. Models in `app/models/search/`.

### Imports and exports

Allow people to move between OSS and SAAS Fizzy instances:
- Exports/Imports can be written to/read from local or S3 storage depending on the config of the instance (both must be supported)
- Must be able to handle very large ZIP files (500+GB)
- Models in `app/models/account/data_transfer/`, `app/models/zip_file`

## Coding style

Before editing or reviewing code, read STYLE.md.
=== STYLE.md ===

# Style

We aim to write code that is a pleasure to read, and we have a lot of opinions about how to do it well. Writing great code is an essential part of our programming culture, and we deliberately set a high bar for every code change anyone contributes. We care about how code reads, how code looks, and how code makes you feel when you read it.

We love discussing code. If you have questions about how to write something, or if you detect some smell you are not quite sure how to solve, please ask away to other programmers. A Pull Request is a great way to do this.

When writing new code, unless you are very familiar with our approach, try to find similar code elsewhere to look for inspiration.

## Conditional returns

In general, we prefer to use expanded conditionals over guard clauses.

```ruby
# Bad
def todos_for_new_group
  ids = params.require(:todolist)[:todo_ids]
  return [] unless ids
  @bucket.recordings.todos.find(ids.split(","))
end

# Good
def todos_for_new_group
  if ids = params.require(:todolist)[:todo_ids]
    @bucket.recordings.todos.find(ids.split(","))
  else
    []
  end
end
```

This is because guard clauses can be hard to read, especially when they are nested.

As an exception, we sometimes use guard clauses to return early from a method:

* When the return is right at the beginning of the method.
* When the main method body is not trivial and involves several lines of code.

```ruby
def after_recorded_as_commit(recording)
  return if recording.parent.was_created?

  if recording.was_created?
    broadcast_new_column(recording)
  else
    broadcast_column_change(recording)
  end
end
```

## Methods ordering

We order methods in classes in the following order:

1. `class` methods
2. `public` methods with `initialize` at the top.
3. `private` methods

- Configurable via Account/Board settings

### UUID Primary Keys

All tables use UUIDs (UUIDv7 format, base36-encoded as 25-char strings):
- Custom fixture UUID generation maintains deterministic ordering for tests
- Fixtures are always "older" than runtime records
- `.first`/`.last` work correctly in tests

### Background Jobs (Solid Queue)

Database-backed job queue (no Redis):
- Custom `FizzyActiveJobExtensions` prepended to ActiveJob
- Jobs automatically capture/restore `Current.account`
- Mission Control::Jobs for monitoring

Recurring tasks are declared in `config/recurring.yml`.

### Sharded Full-Text Search

Full-text search runs in the database, not Elasticsearch. On MySQL it is sharded 16 ways by CRC32 of the account ID (`Search::Record::Trilogy`); on SQLite it is a single FTS5 index (`Search::Record::SQLite`). Don't assume the sharded shape when working under SQLite. Models in `app/models/search/`.

### Imports and exports

Allow people to move between OSS and SAAS Fizzy instances:
- Exports/Imports can be written to/read from local or S3 storage depending on the config of the instance (both must be supported)
- Must be able to handle very large ZIP files (500+GB)
- Models in `app/models/account/data_transfer/`, `app/models/zip_file`

## Coding style

Before editing or reviewing code, read STYLE.md.
=== STYLE.md ===

# Style

We aim to write code that is a pleasure to read, and we have a lot of opinions about how to do it well. Writing great code is an essential part of our programming culture, and we deliberately set a high bar for every code change anyone contributes. We care about how code reads, how code looks, and how code makes you feel when you read it.

We love discussing code. If you have questions about how to write something, or if you detect some smell you are not quite sure how to solve, please ask away to other programmers. A Pull Request is a great way to do this.

When writing new code, unless you are very familiar with our approach, try to find similar code elsewhere to look for inspiration.

## Conditional returns

In general, we prefer to use expanded conditionals over guard clauses.

```ruby
# Bad
def todos_for_new_group
  ids = params.require(:todolist)[:todo_ids]
  return [] unless ids
  @bucket.recordings.todos.find(ids.split(","))
end

# Good
def todos_for_new_group
  if ids = params.require(:todolist)[:todo_ids]
    @bucket.recordings.todos.find(ids.split(","))
  else
    []
  end
end
```

This is because guard clauses can be hard to read, especially when they are nested.

As an exception, we sometimes use guard clauses to return early from a method:

* When the return is right at the beginning of the method.
* When the main method body is not trivial and involves several lines of code.

```ruby
def after_recorded_as_commit(recording)
  return if recording.parent.was_created?

  if recording.was_created?
    broadcast_new_column(recording)
  else
    broadcast_column_change(recording)
  end
end
```

## Methods ordering

We order methods in classes in the following order:

1. `class` methods
2. `public` methods with `initialize` at the top.
3. `private` methods

# Fizzy SaaS

37signals' hosted Fizzy: billing, our production setup, our deploy destinations. Apply this only when SaaS mode is enabled — the root `AGENTS.md` has the check.

`bin/rails saas:enable` creates `tmp/saas.txt`; `bin/rails saas:disable` removes it. `Fizzy.saas?` also reads `SAAS` from the environment, where anything but `false` enables and `SAAS=false` forces off even with the file present (`lib/fizzy.rb`) — that path is for the production image and `bin/ci`, not for switching a checkout. Enabling swaps the bundle to `Gemfile.saas` and the default database adapter to MySQL, so it changes what every `bin/rails` and `bin/kamal` command does.

`README.md` covers the environments, Stripe, push credentials, and maintenance mode. What it doesn't say:

`saas:enable` is a prerequisite for deploying, not just for local development. Only under that flag does `bin/kamal` pass `-c` pointing at this gem's `config/deploy.yml`. Skip it and Kamal reads the root `config/deploy.yml` instead — the self-hosting example, which knows nothing about our destinations.

## Deploy

Pre-deploy: `bin/rails saas:enable`
Deploy: `bin/kamal deploy -d <destination>`
Destinations: production, staging, beta, beta1

One `saas/config/deploy.<destination>.yml` each — paths here are given from the repository root, because that's where you're working from, and `config/deploy.yml` at the root is the self-hosting example rather than ours. `beta` is a template requiring the `BETA_NUMBER` env var; `beta1` is the only numbered target that exists. The `saas/.kamal/secrets.beta2` through `saas/.kamal/secrets.beta4` symlinks are leftovers and don't make those destinations real.

The default branch stays in the root `AGENTS.md` — it describes the repository, not the hosted deployment.

To make Fizzy run in SaaS mode, run this in the terminal:

To go back to open source mode:

```ruby
bin/rails saas:disable
```

## How to update Fizzy

After making changes to this gem, you need to update Fizzy to pick up the changes:

```ruby
BUNDLE_GEMFILE=Gemfile.saas bundle update --conservative fizzy-saas
```

## Working with Stripe

The first time, you need to:

1. Install Stripe CLI: https://stripe.com/docs/stripe-cli
2. Run `stripe login` and authorize the environment `37signals Development`

Then, for working on the Stripe integration locally, you need to run this script to start the tunneling and set the environment variables:

```sh
eval "$(BUNDLE_GEMFILE=Gemfile.saas bundle exec stripe-dev)"
bin/dev # You need to start the dev server in the same terminal session
```

This will ask for your 1password authorization to read and set the environment variables that Stripe needs.

### Stripe environments

* [Development](https://dashboard.stripe.com/acct_1SdTFtRus34tgjsJ/test/dashboard)
* [Staging](https://dashboard.stripe.com/acct_1SdTbuRvb8txnPBR/test/dashboard)
* [Production](https://dashboard.stripe.com/acct_1SNy97RwChFE4it8/dashboard)

## Working with Push Notifications

To test native push notifications (APNs and FCM) locally, start the dev server with the `--push` flag:

```sh
bin/dev --push
```

This will ask for your 1Password authorization to fetch the push credentials. Note that this loads the **production** APNs and FCM credentials into your environment.

## Environments

Fizzy is deployed with [Kamal](https://kamal-deploy.org/). You'll need to have the 1Password CLI set up in order to access the secrets that are used when deploying. Provided you have that, it should be as simple as `bin/kamal deploy` to the correct environment.

## Handbook

See the [Fizzy handbook](https://handbooks.37signals.works/18/fizzy) for runbooks and more.

### Production

- https://app.fizzy.do/

This environment uses a FlashBlade bucket for blob storage.

Beta is primarily intended for testing product features. It uses the same production database and Active Storage configuration.

There is 1 beta environment:

- https://beta1.fizzy-beta.com

Deploy with: `bin/kamal deploy -d beta1`

### Staging

Staging is primarily intended for testing infrastructure changes. It uses production-like but separate database and Active Storage configurations.

- https://app.fizzy-staging.com/

## Maintenance mode

To take production offline for maintenance, run `kamal-proxy stop` on the load balancers via `knife ssh`:

```bash
knife ssh 'hostname:fizzy-lb-*' "sudo docker exec fizzy-load-balancer kamal-proxy stop fizzy --message='Sorry! Fizzy is undergoing some maintenance and will be back shortly.'"
```

Verify maintenance is enabled by visiting https://app.fizzy.do/.

To lift maintenance mode:

```bash
knife ssh 'hostname:fizzy-lb-*' 'sudo docker exec fizzy-load-balancer kamal-proxy resume fizzy'
```

fizzy-saas is released under the [O'Saasy License](LICENSE.md).

module Fizzy
  class << self
    def saas?
      return @saas if defined?(@saas)
      @saas = !!(((ENV["SAAS"] || File.exist?(File.expand_path("../tmp/saas.txt", __dir__))) && ENV["SAAS"] != "false"))
    end

    def db_adapter
      @db_adapter ||= DbAdapter.new ENV.fetch("DATABASE_ADAPTER", saas? ? "mysql" : "sqlite")
    end

    def configure_bundle
      if saas?
        ENV["BUNDLE_GEMFILE"] = "Gemfile.saas"
      end
    end
  end

  class DbAdapter
    def initialize(name)
      @name = name.to_s
    end

    def to_s
      @name
    end

    # Not using inquiry so that it works before Rails env loads.
    def sqlite?
      @name == "sqlite"
    end
  end
end

require_relative "../../rails_ext/active_record_tasks_database_tasks.rb"

module Fizzy
  module Saas
    class Engine < ::Rails::Engine
      # moved from config/initializers/queenbee.rb
      Queenbee.host_app = Fizzy

      # Configure ActionPushNative to use the saas database
      ActiveSupport.on_load(:action_push_native_record) do
        connects_to database: { writing: :saas, reading: :saas }
      end

      initializer "fizzy_saas.assets" do |app|
        app.config.assets.paths << root.join("app/assets/stylesheets")
      end

      initializer "fizzy_saas.public_files" do |app|
        app.middleware.insert_after ActionDispatch::Static, ActionDispatch::Static, root.join("public").to_s,
          headers: app.config.public_file_server.headers
      end

      initializer "fizzy_saas.push_config", after: "action_push_native.config" do |app|
        app.paths["config/push"].unshift(root.join("config/push.yml").to_s)
      end

      initializer "fizzy.saas.mount" do |app|
        app.routes.append do
          mount Fizzy::Saas::Engine => "/", as: "saas"
        end
      end

      initializer "fizzy_saas.transaction_pinning" do |app|
        # GTID-based pinning is a MySQL replication concern; without a replica
        # topology there is nothing to pin.
        unless Fizzy.db_adapter.sqlite?
          app.config.middleware.insert_after(ActiveRecord::Middleware::DatabaseSelector, TransactionPinning::Middleware)
        end
      end

      initializer "fizzy_saas.true_client_ip" do |app|
        app.config.middleware.insert_before ActionDispatch::RemoteIp, TrackTrueClientIp
      end

      initializer "fizzy_saas.gvl_instrumentation" do |app|
        app.config.middleware.insert_before(Rack::Runtime, GvlInstrumentation)
      end

      initializer "fizzy_saas.solid_queue" do
        SolidQueue.on_start do
          Process.warmup

        end
      end

      initializer "fizzy_saas.logging.session" do |app|
        ActiveSupport.on_load(:action_controller_base) do
          before_action do

module Account::StorageLimited
  extend ActiveSupport::Concern

  DEFAULT_STORAGE_LIMIT = 1.gigabyte
  NEAR_STORAGE_LIMIT_THRESHOLD = 500.megabytes

  included do
    has_one :storage_exception
  end

  def storage_limit
    storage_exception&.bytes_allowed || DEFAULT_STORAGE_LIMIT
  end

  def exceeding_storage_limit?
    bytes_used > storage_limit
  end

  def nearing_storage_limit?
    !exceeding_storage_limit? && bytes_used > storage_limit - NEAR_STORAGE_LIMIT_THRESHOLD
  end

  def add_storage_exception(bytes)
    if storage_exception
      storage_exception.update!(bytes_allowed: bytes)
    else
      create_storage_exception!(bytes_allowed: bytes)
    end
  end
end

class ApplicationPushNotification < ActionPushNative::Notification
  queue_as :default

  class << self
    # Native push runs only where APNs/FCM credentials are provisioned: production
    # and beta. Staging is deliberately unprovisioned, so it enqueues no-op jobs.
    # ENABLE_NATIVE_PUSH=true is the escape hatch for development (via exe/push-dev)
    # or any environment that gets credentials later.
    def enable?
      Rails.env.production? || Rails.env.beta? || ENV["ENABLE_NATIVE_PUSH"] == "true"
    end

    def verify_credentials!
      config = ActionPushNative.config

      { "APNS_KEY_ID" => config.dig(:apple, :key_id),
        "APNS_ENCRYPTION_KEY_B64" => config.dig(:apple, :encryption_key),
        "FCM_ENCRYPTION_KEY_B64" => config.dig(:google, :encryption_key) }.each do |env_var, value|
        raise "Native push is enabled but #{env_var} is not set" if value.blank?
      end
    end
  end

  self.enabled = enable?
  verify_credentials! if enabled
end

  def process
    if devices.any?
      native_notification.deliver_later_to(devices)
    end
  end

    def devices
      @devices ||= notification.identity.devices
    end

      ApplicationPushNotification
        .with_apple(
          aps: {
            category: payload.category,
            "mutable-content": 1,
            "interruption-level": interruption_level
          }
        )
        .with_google(
          android: { notification: nil }
        )
        .with_data(
          title: payload.title,
          body: payload.body,
          url: payload.url,
          base_url: payload.base_url,
          account_id: notification.account.id,
          account_slug: notification.account.slug,
          avatar_url: payload.avatar_url,

          creator_initials: notification.creator.initials,
          creator_avatar_color: notification.creator.avatar_background_color,
          category: payload.category
        )
        .new(

          sound: "default",

module Account::StorageLimited
  extend ActiveSupport::Concern

  DEFAULT_STORAGE_LIMIT = 1.gigabyte
  NEAR_STORAGE_LIMIT_THRESHOLD = 500.megabytes

  included do
    has_one :storage_exception
  end

  def storage_limit
    storage_exception&.bytes_allowed || DEFAULT_STORAGE_LIMIT
  end

  def exceeding_storage_limit?
    bytes_used > storage_limit
  end

  def nearing_storage_limit?
    !exceeding_storage_limit? && bytes_used > storage_limit - NEAR_STORAGE_LIMIT_THRESHOLD
  end

  def add_storage_exception(bytes)
    if storage_exception
      storage_exception.update!(bytes_allowed: bytes)
    else
      create_storage_exception!(bytes_allowed: bytes)
    end
  end
end

class ApplicationPushNotification < ActionPushNative::Notification
  queue_as :default

  class << self
    # Native push runs only where APNs/FCM credentials are provisioned: production
    # and beta. Staging is deliberately unprovisioned, so it enqueues no-op jobs.
    # ENABLE_NATIVE_PUSH=true is the escape hatch for development (via exe/push-dev)
    # or any environment that gets credentials later.
    def enable?
      Rails.env.production? || Rails.env.beta? || ENV["ENABLE_NATIVE_PUSH"] == "true"
    end

    def verify_credentials!
      config = ActionPushNative.config

      { "APNS_KEY_ID" => config.dig(:apple, :key_id),
        "APNS_ENCRYPTION_KEY_B64" => config.dig(:apple, :encryption_key),
        "FCM_ENCRYPTION_KEY_B64" => config.dig(:google, :encryption_key) }.each do |env_var, value|
        raise "Native push is enabled but #{env_var} is not set" if value.blank?
      end
    end
  end

  self.enabled = enable?
  verify_credentials! if enabled
end

class Notification::PushTarget::Native < Notification::PushTarget
  def process
    if devices.any?
      native_notification.deliver_later_to(devices)
    end
  end

  private
    def devices
      @devices ||= notification.identity.devices
    end

    def payload
      @payload ||= notification.payload
    end

    def native_notification
      ApplicationPushNotification
        .with_apple(
          aps: {
            category: payload.category,
            "mutable-content": 1,
            "interruption-level": interruption_level
          }
        )
        .with_google(
          android: { notification: nil }
        )
        .with_data(
          title: payload.title,
          body: payload.body,
          url: payload.url,
          base_url: payload.base_url,
          account_id: notification.account.id,
          account_slug: notification.account.slug,
          avatar_url: payload.avatar_url,
          card_id: card&.id,
          card_title: card&.title,
          creator_id: notification.creator.id,
          creator_name: notification.creator.name,
          creator_familiar_name: notification.creator.familiar_name,
          creator_initials: notification.creator.initials,
          creator_avatar_color: notification.creator.avatar_background_color,
          category: payload.category
        )
        .new(
          title: payload.title,
          body: payload.body,
          badge: notification.user.notifications.unread.count,
          sound: "default",
          thread_id: card&.id,
          high_priority: payload.high_priority?
        )
    end

    def interruption_level
      payload.high_priority? ? "time-sensitive" : "active"
    end
end

require "test_helper"

class Admin::AuditsControllerTest < ActionDispatch::IntegrationTest
  # Test authentication via the Audits1984::SessionsController#index endpoint,
  # which inherits from Admin::AuditsController through Audits1984::ApplicationController.

  test "unauthenticated access is forbidden" do
    untenanted do
      get saas.admin_audits1984_path
      assert_redirected_to new_session_path
    end
  end

  test "logged-in non-staff access is forbidden" do
    sign_in_as :jz

    untenanted do
      get saas.admin_audits1984_path
    end

    assert_response :forbidden
  end

  test "logged-in staff access is allowed" do
    sign_in_as :david

    untenanted do
      get saas.admin_audits1984_path
    end

    assert_response :success
  end

  test "invalid bearer token is forbidden" do
    untenanted do
      get saas.admin_audits1984_path, headers: { "Authorization" => "Bearer invalid_token" }
    end

    assert_response :unauthorized
  end

  test "valid bearer token is allowed" do
    token = Audits1984::AuditorToken.generate_for(identities(:david))

    untenanted do
      get saas.admin_audits1984_path, headers: { "Authorization" => "Bearer #{token}" }

    assert_response :success

  end

require "test_helper"
require "queenbee/testing/client"

class Account::QueenbeeIntegrationTest < ActiveSupport::TestCase
  include Queenbee::Testing::Client

  # Fizzy creates accounts via its own Signup flow (Fizzy → Queenbee),
  # not via Queenbee pushing to Fizzy, so create_with_dependents is N/A.
  undef_method :test_client_class_should_respond_to_create_with_dependents

  setup do
    @account = accounts(:"37s")
  end

  test "find_by_queenbee_id looks up by external_account_id" do
    assert_equal @account, Account.find_by_queenbee_id(@account.external_account_id)
  end

  test "queenbee_id returns external_account_id" do
    assert_equal @account.external_account_id, @account.queenbee_id
  end

  test "cancel! creates cancellation attributed to system user" do
    @account.cancel!

    assert @account.cancelled?
    assert_equal @account.system_user, @account.cancellation.initiated_by
  end

  test "cancel! is idempotent" do
    @account.cancel!
    assert_no_difference -> { Account::Cancellation.count } do
      @account.cancel!
    end
  end

  test "cancel and reactivate round-trips" do
    @account.cancel!
    assert_not @account.active?

    @account.reactivate!
    @account.reload
    assert @account.active?
  end

  test "deactivate! cancels the account" do
    @account.deactivate!
    assert @account.cancelled?
  end

    assert_equal users(:jason).name, @account.owner_name
    assert_equal "jason@37signals.com", @account.owner_email
  end

  test "comped= is a no-op" do
    @account.comped = true
    assert_not @account.comped?
  end

  test "transferred_ownership! raises NotImplementedError" do
    assert_raises(NotImplementedError) { @account.transferred_ownership! }
  end

  test "qb_serializable_hash includes queenbee_id and subscription" do
    hash = @account.qb_serializable_hash
    assert_equal @account.external_account_id, hash[:id]
    assert_equal({ quantity: 1 }, hash[:subscription])
  end
end

require "test_helper"
require "queenbee/testing/client"

class Account::QueenbeeIntegrationTest < ActiveSupport::TestCase
  include Queenbee::Testing::Client

  # Fizzy creates accounts via its own Signup flow (Fizzy → Queenbee),
  # not via Queenbee pushing to Fizzy, so create_with_dependents is N/A.
  undef_method :test_client_class_should_respond_to_create_with_dependents

  setup do
    @account = accounts(:"37s")
  end

  test "find_by_queenbee_id looks up by external_account_id" do
    assert_equal @account, Account.find_by_queenbee_id(@account.external_account_id)
  end

  test "queenbee_id returns external_account_id" do
    assert_equal @account.external_account_id, @account.queenbee_id
  end

  test "cancel! creates cancellation attributed to system user" do
    @account.cancel!

    assert @account.cancelled?
    assert_equal @account.system_user, @account.cancellation.initiated_by
  end

  test "cancel! is idempotent" do
    @account.cancel!
    assert_no_difference -> { Account::Cancellation.count } do
      @account.cancel!
    end
  end

  test "cancel and reactivate round-trips" do
    @account.cancel!
    assert_not @account.active?

    @account.reactivate!
    @account.reload
    assert @account.active?
  end

  test "deactivate! cancels the account" do
    @account.deactivate!
    assert @account.cancelled?
  end

  test "owner_name and owner_email from account owner" do
    assert_equal users(:jason).name, @account.owner_name
    assert_equal "jason@37signals.com", @account.owner_email
  end

  test "comped= is a no-op" do
    @account.comped = true
    assert_not @account.comped?
  end

  test "transferred_ownership! raises NotImplementedError" do
    assert_raises(NotImplementedError) { @account.transferred_ownership! }
  end

  test "qb_serializable_hash includes queenbee_id and subscription" do
    hash = @account.qb_serializable_hash
    assert_equal @account.external_account_id, hash[:id]
    assert_equal({ quantity: 1 }, hash[:subscription])
  end
end

require "test_helper"

class Account::StorageExceptionTest < ActiveSupport::TestCase
  test "storage limit returns default when no exception exists" do
    assert_equal Account::StorageLimited::DEFAULT_STORAGE_LIMIT, accounts(:initech).storage_limit
  end

  test "storage limit returns exception value when one exists" do
    account = accounts(:initech)
    account.add_storage_exception(5.gigabytes)

    assert_equal 5.gigabytes, account.storage_limit
  end

  test "add storage exception creates a new record" do
    account = accounts(:initech)

    assert_difference -> { Account::StorageException.count } do
      account.add_storage_exception(2.gigabytes)
    end

    assert_equal 2.gigabytes, account.storage_exception.bytes_allowed
  end

  test "add storage exception updates existing record" do
    account = accounts(:initech)
    account.add_storage_exception(2.gigabytes)

    assert_no_difference -> { Account::StorageException.count } do
      account.add_storage_exception(10.gigabytes)
    end

    assert_equal 10.gigabytes, account.storage_exception.reload.bytes_allowed
  end

  test "exceeding storage limit respects exception" do
    account = accounts(:initech)
    Account.any_instance.stubs(:bytes_used).returns(2.gigabytes)

    assert account.exceeding_storage_limit?

    account.add_storage_exception(5.gigabytes)

    assert_not account.exceeding_storage_limit?
  end
end

module Authentication
  extend ActiveSupport::Concern

  included do
    before_action :require_account # Checking and setting account must happen first
    before_action :require_authentication
    helper_method :authenticated?
    helper_method :email_address_pending_authentication

    etag { Current.identity.id if authenticated? }

    include Authentication::ViaMagicLink, LoginHelper
  end

  class_methods do
    def require_unauthenticated_access(**options)
      allow_unauthenticated_access **options
      before_action :redirect_authenticated_user, **options
    end

    def allow_unauthenticated_access(**options)
      skip_before_action :require_authentication, **options
      before_action :resume_session, **options
      allow_unauthorized_access **options
    end

    def disallow_account_scope(**options)
      skip_before_action :require_account, **options
      before_action :redirect_tenanted_request, **options
    end
  end

  private
    def authenticated?
      Current.identity.present?
    end

    def require_account
      unless Current.account.present?
        redirect_to main_app.session_menu_path(script_name: nil)
      end
    end

    def require_authentication
      resume_session || authenticate_by_bearer_token || request_authentication
    end

    def resume_session
      if session = find_session_by_cookie
        set_current_session session
      end
    end

    def find_session_by_cookie
      Session.find_signed(cookies.signed[:session_token])
    end

    def authenticate_by_bearer_token
      if request.authorization.to_s.include?("Bearer")
        if bearer_token_authenticatable_request?
          authenticate_or_request_with_http_token do |token|
            if identity = Identity.find_by_permissable_access_token(token, method: request.method)
              Current.identity = identity
            end
          end
        else
          request_http_token_authentication
        end
      end
    end

    def bearer_token_authenticatable_request?
      request.format.json?
    end

    def request_authentication
      if Current.account.present?
        session[:return_to_after_authenticating] = request.url
      end

      redirect_to_login_url
    end

    def after_authentication_url
      session.delete(:return_to_after_authenticating) || landing_url
    end

    def redirect_authenticated_user
      redirect_to main_app.root_url if authenticated?
    end

    def redirect_tenanted_request
      redirect_to main_app.root_url if Current.account.present?
    end

    def start_new_session_for(identity)
      identity.sessions.create!(user_agent: request.user_agent, ip_address: request.remote_ip).tap do |session|
        set_current_session session
      end
    end

    def set_current_session(session)
      Current.session = session
      cookies.signed.permanent[:session_token] = { value: session.signed_id, httponly: true, same_site: :lax }
    end

    def terminate_session
      Current.session.destroy
      cookies.delete(:session_token)
    end

    def session_token
      cookies[:session_token]
    end

    before_action :require_authentication
    helper_method :authenticated?
    helper_method :email_address_pending_authentication

    etag { Current.identity.id if authenticated? }

    include Authentication::ViaMagicLink, LoginHelper
  end

  class_methods do
    def require_unauthenticated_access(**options)
      allow_unauthenticated_access **options
      before_action :redirect_authenticated_user, **options
    end

    def allow_unauthenticated_access(**options)
      skip_before_action :require_authentication, **options
      before_action :resume_session, **options
      allow_unauthorized_access **options
    end

    def disallow_account_scope(**options)
      skip_before_action :require_account, **options
      before_action :redirect_tenanted_request, **options
    end
  end

  private
    def authenticated?
      Current.identity.present?
    end

    def require_account
      unless Current.account.present?
        redirect_to main_app.session_menu_path(script_name: nil)
      end
    end

    def require_authentication
      resume_session || authenticate_by_bearer_token || request_authentication
    end

    def resume_session
      if session = find_session_by_cookie
        set_current_session session
      end
    end

    def find_session_by_cookie
      Session.find_signed(cookies.signed[:session_token])
    end

    def authenticate_by_bearer_token
      if request.authorization.to_s.include?("Bearer")
        if bearer_token_authenticatable_request?
          authenticate_or_request_with_http_token do |token|
            if identity = Identity.find_by_permissable_access_token(token, method: request.method)
              Current.identity = identity
            end
          end
        else
          request_http_token_authentication
        end
      end
    end

    def bearer_token_authenticatable_request?
      request.format.json?
    end

    def request_authentication
      if Current.account.present?
        session[:return_to_after_authenticating] = request.url
      end

      redirect_to_login_url
    end

    def after_authentication_url
      session.delete(:return_to_after_authenticating) || landing_url
    end

    def redirect_authenticated_user
      redirect_to main_app.root_url if authenticated?
    end

    def redirect_tenanted_request
      redirect_to main_app.root_url if Current.account.present?
    end

    def start_new_session_for(identity)
      identity.sessions.create!(user_agent: request.user_agent, ip_address: request.remote_ip).tap do |session|
        set_current_session session
      end
    end

    def set_current_session(session)
      Current.session = session
      cookies.signed.permanent[:session_token] = { value: session.signed_id, httponly: true, same_site: :lax }
    end

    def terminate_session
      Current.session.destroy
      cookies.delete(:session_token)
    end

    def session_token
      cookies[:session_token]
    end
end

messages.thinking:
**API Version Shenanigans and the Perils of `try`**

Whoa, this is a major gotcha! I'm staring at this API version: `API_VERSION: 2026-02-25.clover`. And the implications are significant. It looks like Stripe decided to play with the `current_period_end` field in their subscription object. Specifically, in versions from `2025-03-31.basil` onwards, including this current one, `current_period_end` is no longer directly at `subscription.current_period_end`. Instead, it's buried deeper, nested within `subscription.items.data.first.current_period_end`. That's going to break a lot of integrations!

Then I'm thinking about the Ruby code and the potential for errors. Specifically I'm pondering `Stripe::Subscription` compared with using `try`. In standard Ruby (without ActiveSupport), the `try` method isn't defined, which means your code could blow up with a `NoMethodError` if you just assumed it was available. But wait, `Stripe::StripeObject` uses `method_missing` and `[]` for accessing attributes! So, `stripe_sub[:current_period_end]` will *return* `nil` if the key is missing, rather than throw an error. That's a critical difference. It's a key distinction between implicit nil and a raised error.

I think I need to test that `StripeObject` behavior more rigorously, particularly considering ActiveSupport's influence on the situation. I'll need to run this code with ActiveSupport loaded, like in a `rails runner` context, or by requiring `"active_support/all"` to make sure I'm capturing the proper behavior in my tests. It's important to understand *exactly* how the framework and Stripe's library interact with those nil values.

messages.thinking:
**A Eureka Moment: Unraveling the Account Overridden Limits System**

Okay, so I've been presented with a challenge: implement an admin override system for account limits. Initially, I was looking at the basic structure and how it connects to the admin interface. Seeing the migrations for the `account_overridden_limits` table (`card_count`, `bytes_used`) was a vital clue. But now, it's crystal clear!

I immediately saw the connection to the core usage metrics: card count and bytes used. These are the two key values checked against account plans. The core of this functionality lies in how these limits are *actually* applied. It all revolves around this separate `account_overridden_limits` table.

I realized that we *can't* directly modify `accounts.cards_count`. The reason is the auto-incrementing sequential card numbers. So, if we adjust the used card count, we will break the card generation in `Card#assign_number`. Similarly, `storage_totals.bytes_stored` are updated via background jobs and shouldn't be touched directly. This is precisely why `account_overridden_limits` exists! It creates a way to *simulate* different limit scenarios! The code will check the `overridden_limits&.card_count` and `overridden_limits&.bytes_used` and use the overridden values, *only* when the overridden limit is active.

And the beauty of it is the clean architecture. The concerns handle the usage: with the overridden limit set, the code would be transparent. The key is how the `bytes_used` method is overridden when `overridden_limits` exist. Since `bytes_used` is called by `exceeding_storage_limit?` and `nearing_storage_limit?`, the logic works perfectly, overriding the behavior *conditionally* without disrupting other storage processes. The fact that the `bytes_used` and `card_count` methods are defined in concerns and effectively overridden by the presence of `account_overridden_limits` is a stroke of genius! I think the usage of `||` is brilliant.

I'm confident we have a well-designed solution. Now, I need to verify that we are not breaking any functionality in any of the tests! I think I'll look over those storage tests, just to be *completely* certain. I want to be 100% positive that the test suite continues to function correctly, particularly those related to storage totals.

**Stripe Webhook and Billing Architecture Deep Dive**

Okay, here's the breakdown of my thinking on this Stripe integration.  First, let's nail down webhook security.  The `webhook_secret` check is critical; if it's blank, that `construct_event` method throws an error, which we need to catch. Returning a `head :bad_request` (or even service_unavailable for a more robust handling)  handles this cleanly. We also need to rescue `JSON::ParserError` AND `Stripe::SignatureVerificationError`.  I realized that `construct_event` checks the signature BEFORE parsing the JSON, so this dual rescue handles both possible failure points elegantly.

Now, for handling Stripe events in the `Stripe::WebhooksController#create` controller.  We need to make sure we're handling ALL relevant billing events, which can be done with the following:
*   `customer.subscription.created`, `updated`, and `deleted`:  These need to trigger a sync of the subscription data.  The updated event is particularly complex, handling plan upgrades, downgrades, cancellations, and status changes. The deleted event is important to handle cancelling the subscription and setting the status back to free.
*   `checkout.session.completed`:  This is where the initial subscription link is made between the account and customer. The metadata is key here and making sure we can handle the case where the session completes BEFORE the `customer.subscription.created` event arrives.
*   `invoice.upcoming`, `invoice.payment_succeeded`, etc.: We need to make sure we're updating `next_amount_due_in_cents` from the invoice data if there's a subscription.
*   Unrecognized events: For any unknown event types, we need to return a `head :ok` (200) to keep Stripe happy.  This is CRITICAL to prevent webhook retries and endpoint disables.
*   Unknown customer/subscription:  If we get an event for a `stripe_customer_id` / `stripe_subscription_id` that *doesn't* match a local `Account::Subscription`, we need to log a warning but still return a 200.  Don't 500 on unknowns.

Now, for those lookups: The `find_or_build_subscription` method!  We need to look at how we're finding the subscription records.  Using the `stripe_subscription_id` is the primary key.  Also, if that fails, we can find it by the `stripe_customer_id`. The metadata is also key, so we need to make sure `metadata[:account_id]` and `metadata[:external_account_id]` are both available. We need to remember that `StripeObject#[]` handles both symbol and string keys for the metadata. We also need to handle the case where the customer ID is an object instead of a string.

And we need to handle the edge case of an old canceled subscription with the same customer ID as a new, active one!  We need to make sure we *don't* overwrite the new subscription with the deleted one when the `customer.subscription.deleted` event comes in out of order, which is so production-grade! But `customer.subscription.created` SHOULD overwrite old canceled subscription!

Next, let's move on to the `config/routes.rb` and the routes and controllers for the Stripe Checkout and Billing Portal.

The routes are tenant aware via the `AccountSlug::Extractor`. This means we need to think carefully about the routes and controllers for Stripe Checkout and the Stripe Customer Portal!

The checkout flow itself (`Account::SubscriptionsController`) needs to do a few things, especially:

{

# Define an application-wide Content Security Policy.
# https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Headers/Content-Security-Policy
#
# Directives are configurable via environment variables with fallback to config.x
# settings. This allows fizzy-saas (or other deployments) to extend the base policy
# without duplicating it.
#
# ENV vars (space-separated sources):
#   CSP_DEFAULT_SRC, CSP_SCRIPT_SRC, CSP_STYLE_SRC, CSP_CONNECT_SRC, CSP_FRAME_SRC,
#   CSP_IMG_SRC, CSP_FONT_SRC, CSP_MEDIA_SRC, CSP_WORKER_SRC, CSP_FRAME_ANCESTORS,
#   CSP_FORM_ACTION, CSP_REPORT_URI, CSP_REPORT_ONLY, DISABLE_CSP
#
# config.x.content_security_policy.* (string, space-separated string, or array):
#   script_src, style_src, connect_src, frame_src, img_src, font_src, media_src,
#   worker_src, frame_ancestors, form_action, report_uri, report_only

Rails.application.configure do
  # Helper to get additional CSP sources from ENV or config.x.
  # Supports: nil, string, space-separated string, or array.
  sources = ->(directive) do
    env_key = "CSP_#{directive.to_s.upcase}"
    value = if ENV.key?(env_key)
      ENV[env_key]
    else
      config.x.content_security_policy.send(directive)
    end

    case value
    when nil then []
    when Array then value
    when String then value.split
    else []
    end
  end

  # Report URI and report-only mode
  report_uri = ENV.fetch("CSP_REPORT_URI") { config.x.content_security_policy.report_uri }
  report_only =
    if ENV.key?("CSP_REPORT_ONLY")
      ENV["CSP_REPORT_ONLY"] == "true"
    else
      config.x.content_security_policy.report_only
    end

  # Generate nonces for importmap and inline scripts
  config.content_security_policy_nonce_generator = ->(request) { SecureRandom.base64(16) }
  config.content_security_policy_nonce_directives = %w[ script-src ]

  config.content_security_policy do |policy|
    policy.default_src :self, *sources.(:default_src)
    policy.script_src :self, *sources.(:script_src)
    policy.connect_src :self, *sources.(:connect_src)
    policy.frame_src :self, *sources.(:frame_src)

    # Don't fight user tools: permit inline styles, data:/https: sources, and
    # blob: workers for accessibility extensions, privacy tools, and custom fonts.
    policy.style_src :self, :unsafe_inline, *sources.(:style_src)
    policy.img_src :self, "blob:", "data:", "https:", *sources.(:img_src)
    policy.font_src :self, "data:", "https:", *sources.(:font_src)
    policy.media_src :self, "blob:", "data:", "https:", *sources.(:media_src)
    policy.worker_src :self, "blob:", *sources.(:worker_src)

    # Security-critical defaults (not configurable)
    policy.object_src :none
    policy.base_uri :none

    policy.form_action :self, *sources.(:form_action)
    policy.frame_ancestors :self, *sources.(:frame_ancestors)

    # Specify URI for violation reports (e.g., Sentry CSP endpoint)
    policy.report_uri report_uri if report_uri
  end

  # Report violations without enforcing the policy.
  config.content_security_policy_report_only = report_only
end unless ENV["DISABLE_CSP"]
"
}

  config.content_security_policy_nonce_directives = %w[ script-src ]

    policy.default_src :self, *sources.(:default_src)
    policy.script_src :self, *sources.(:script_src)
    policy.connect_src :self, *sources.(:connect_src)
    policy.frame_src :self, *sources.(:frame_src)

    policy.base_uri :none

    policy.frame_ancestors :self, *sources.(:frame_ancestors)

    policy.report_uri report_uri if report_uri
  end

    free_v1: {
      name: "Free",
      price: 0,
      card_limit: 1_000,
      storage_limit: 1.gigabyte,
      stripe_price_id_env: nil

      name: "Unlimited+",
      price: 25,
      card_limit: Float::INFINITY,
      storage_limit: 500.gigabytes,
      stripe_price_id_env: "STRIPE_MONTHLY_EXTRA_STORAGE_V1_PRICE_ID"
    }
  }.freeze

  class << self
    def all
      @all ||= PLANS.map { |key, attributes| new(key: key, **attributes) }.freeze
    end

    def paid_plans
      all.select(&:paid?)
    end

    def free

    end

    def paid

    def extra_storage

    def find(key)

      all.find { |plan| plan.key == key.to_sym }
    end

    def find_by_price_id(price_id)

      all.find { |plan| plan.stripe_price_id.present? && plan.stripe_price_id == price_id }

  end

  attr_reader :key, :name, :price, :card_limit, :storage_limit

  def free?

class Account::Subscription < SaasRecord
  ACTIVE_STATUSES = %w[ active trialing past_due ].freeze

  belongs_to :account

  validates :stripe_customer_id, presence: true, uniqueness: true
  validates :stripe_subscription_id, uniqueness: true, allow_nil: true

  scope :active, -> { where(status: ACTIVE_STATUSES) }

  def plan
    Plan.find(plan_key) || Plan.free
  end

  def active?
    status.in?(ACTIVE_STATUSES)
  end

  def paid?
    active? && plan.paid?
  end

  def canceled?
    status == "canceled"
  end

  def past_due?
    status == "past_due"
  end

  def paused?
    status == "paused"
  end

  def to_be_canceled?
    active? && cancel_at.present?
  end

  def sync_from_stripe(stripe_subscription)
    item = stripe_subscription[:items]&.data&.first
    price_id = item&.[](:price)&.id || item&.[](:plan)&.id
    matched_plan = Plan.find_by_price_id(price_id) || Plan.find(stripe_subscription[:metadata]&.[](:plan_key))
    period_end = item&.[](:current_period_end) || stripe_subscription[:current_period_end]
    cancel_at_ts = stripe_subscription[:cancel_at]
    cancel_at_ts ||= period_end if stripe_subscription[:cancel_at_period_end]
    new_status = stripe_subscription[:status].presence || status

    update!(
      stripe_subscription_id: stripe_subscription.id,
      status: new_status,
      plan_key: matched_plan ? matched_plan.key.to_s : plan_key,
      current_period_end: period_end ? Time.at(period_end).utc : current_period_end,
      cancel_at: cancel_at_ts ? Time.at(cancel_at_ts).utc : nil,
      next_amount_due_in_cents: resolve_next_amount_due_in_cents(new_status, item, matched_plan)
    )
  end

  def cancel_in_stripe
    return if stripe_subscription_id.blank?

    Stripe.api_key ||= ENV["STRIPE_SECRET_KEY"]
    Stripe::Subscription.cancel(stripe_subscription_id)
  rescue Stripe::InvalidRequestError => e
    raise unless e.code == "resource_missing" || e.message.to_s.include?("already canceled")
  end

  private
    def resolve_next_amount_due_in_cents(new_status, item, matched_plan)
      if new_status == "canceled"
        nil
      else
        item&.[](:price)&.[](:unit_amount) || (matched_plan ? matched_plan.price * 100 : next_amount_due_in_cents)
      end
    end
end
EOF

module Account::Billing
  extend ActiveSupport::Concern

  NEAR_CARD_LIMIT_THRESHOLD = 100

  included do
    has_one :subscription, class_name: "Account::Subscription", dependent: :destroy
    has_one :billing_waiver, class_name: "Account::BillingWaiver", dependent: :destroy
    has_one :overridden_limits, class_name: "Account::OverriddenLimits", dependent: :destroy

    set_callback :cancel, :after, :cancel_subscription_later
  end

  def active_subscription
    subscription if subscription&.active?
  end

  def plan
    if active_subscription&.paid?
      active_subscription.plan
    elsif comped?
      Plan.paid
    else
      Plan.free
    end
  end

  def paid?
    plan.paid?
  end

  def free?
    plan.free?
  end

  def comped?
    billing_waiver.present?
  end

  def comp
    billing_waiver || create_billing_waiver!
  end

  def uncomp
    billing_waiver&.destroy
    self.billing_waiver = nil
  end

  def comped=(value)
    if ActiveModel::Type::Boolean.new.cast(value)
      comp
    else
      uncomp
    end
  end

  def card_count
    overridden_limits&.card_count || cards_count
  end

  def card_limit
    plan.card_limit
  end

  def cards_remaining
    if plan.limit_cards?
      [ card_limit - card_count, 0 ].max
    else
      Float::INFINITY
    end
  end

  def exceeding_card_limit?
    plan.limit_cards? && card_count >= card_limit
  end

  def nearing_card_limit?
    plan.limit_cards? && !exceeding_card_limit? && cards_remaining <= NEAR_CARD_LIMIT_THRESHOLD
  end

  def bytes_used
    overridden_limits&.bytes_used || super
  end

  def actual_bytes_used
    storage_total&.bytes_stored || 0
  end

  def override_limits(card_count: nil, bytes_used: nil)
    if card_count.nil? && bytes_used.nil?
      reset_overridden_limits
    else
      record = overridden_limits || build_overridden_limits
      record.update!(card_count: card_count, bytes_used: bytes_used)
      record
    end
  end

  def reset_overridden_limits
    overridden_limits&.destroy
    self.overridden_limits = nil
  end

  private
    def cancel_subscription_later
      if active_subscription&.stripe_subscription_id.present?
        Account::CancelSubscriptionJob.perform_later(self)
      end
    end
end
EOF

module Account::StorageLimited
  extend ActiveSupport::Concern

  DEFAULT_STORAGE_LIMIT = 1.gigabyte
  NEAR_STORAGE_LIMIT_THRESHOLD = 500.megabytes

  included do
    has_one :storage_exception, dependent: :destroy
  end

  def storage_limit
    [ storage_exception&.bytes_allowed, plan.storage_limit ].compact.max
  end

  def exceeding_storage_limit?
    bytes_used > storage_limit
  end

  def nearing_storage_limit?
    !exceeding_storage_limit? && bytes_used > storage_limit - NEAR_STORAGE_LIMIT_THRESHOLD
  end

  def add_storage_exception(bytes)
    if storage_exception

      create_storage_exception!(bytes_allowed: bytes)
    end
  end
end

cat <<'EOF' > saas/app/controllers/stripe/webhooks_controller.rb
class Stripe::WebhooksController < ApplicationController
  disallow_account_scope
  allow_unauthenticated_access
  skip_forgery_protection

  def create
    event = construct_event
    return head :bad_request unless event

    process_event(event)
    head :ok
  end

  private
    def construct_event
      webhook_secret = ENV["STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET"]
      return nil if webhook_secret.blank?

      ::Stripe::Webhook.construct_event(
        request.raw_post,
        request.headers["Stripe-Signature"],
        webhook_secret
      )
    rescue JSON::ParserError, ::Stripe::SignatureVerificationError
      nil
    end

    def process_event(event)
      case event.type
      when "checkout.session.completed"
        handle_checkout_session_completed(event.data.object)
      when "customer.subscription.created", "customer.subscription.updated"
        handle_subscription_change(event.data.object)
      when "customer.subscription.deleted"
        handle_subscription_deleted(event.data.object)
      when "invoice.upcoming", "invoice.payment_succeeded", "invoice.paid", "invoice.payment_failed"
        handle_invoice_event(event.data.object, event.type)
      end
    end

    def handle_checkout_session_completed(session)
      return unless session[:mode] == "subscription" || session[:subscription].present?

      customer_id = extract_id(session[:customer])
      subscription_id = extract_id(session[:subscription])
      return if customer_id.blank?

      subscription = find_or_build_subscription(
        customer_id: customer_id,
        subscription_id: subscription_id,
        metadata: session[:metadata],
        client_reference_id: session[:client_reference_id]
      )
      return unless subscription

      attributes = { stripe_customer_id: customer_id }
      attributes[:stripe_subscription_id] = subscription_id if subscription_id.present?

      if subscription.plan_key.blank? && (plan = Plan.find(session[:metadata]&.[](:plan_key)))
        attributes[:plan_key] = plan.key.to_s
      end

      if subscription.status.blank? && session[:payment_status].in?(%w[ paid no_payment_required ])
        attributes[:status] = "active"
      end

      subscription.update!(attributes)
    end

    def handle_subscription_change(stripe_subscription)
      customer_id = extract_id(stripe_subscription[:customer])
      subscription = find_or_build_subscription(
        customer_id: customer_id,
        subscription_id: stripe_subscription.id,
        metadata: stripe_subscription[:metadata]
      )
      return unless subscription
      return if stale_subscription_event?(subscription, stripe_subscription)

      subscription.sync_from_stripe(stripe_subscription)
    end

    def handle_subscription_deleted(stripe_subscription)
      customer_id = extract_id(stripe_subscription[:customer])
      subscription = find_or_build_subscription(
        customer_id: customer_id,
        subscription_id: stripe_subscription.id,
        metadata: stripe_subscription[:metadata]
      )
      return unless subscription

      if subscription.stripe_subscription_id.present? &&
          subscription.stripe_subscription_id != stripe_subscription.id &&
          subscription.active?
        return
      end

      subscription.sync_from_stripe(stripe_subscription)
      subscription.update!(status: "canceled", next_amount_due_in_cents: nil) unless subscription.canceled?
    end

    def handle_invoice_event(invoice, event_type)
      subscription_id = extract_id(invoice[:subscription]) ||
        extract_id(invoice[:parent]&.[](:subscription_details)&.[](:subscription))
      customer_id = extract_id(invoice[:customer])

      subscription = find_subscription(customer_id: customer_id, subscription_id: subscription_id)
      return unless subscription

      if event_type == "invoice.upcoming" && invoice[:amount_due].present?
        subscription.update!(next_amount_due_in_cents: invoice[:amount_due])
      end
    end

    def stale_subscription_event?(subscription, stripe_subscription)
      subscription.stripe_subscription_id.present? &&
        subscription.stripe_subscription_id != stripe_subscription.id &&
        subscription.active? &&
        !stripe_subscription[:status].in?(Account::Subscription::ACTIVE_STATUSES)
    end

    def find_or_build_subscription(customer_id:, subscription_id: nil, metadata: nil, client_reference_id: nil)
      subscription = find_subscription(customer_id: customer_id, subscription_id: subscription_id)

      if subscription.nil? && customer_id.present?
        if account = find_account(metadata: metadata, client_reference_id: client_reference_id)
          subscription = account.subscription || account.build_subscription(stripe_customer_id: customer_id)
          subscription.stripe_customer_id ||= customer_id
        end
      end

      subscription
    end

    def find_subscription(customer_id:, subscription_id: nil)
      if subscription_id.present?
        Account::Subscription.find_by(stripe_subscription_id: subscription_id)
      end || (Account::Subscription.find_by(stripe_customer_id: customer_id) if customer_id.present?)
    end

    def find_account(metadata:, client_reference_id: nil)
      account_id = metadata&.[](:account_id).presence || client_reference_id.presence
      external_account_id = metadata&.[](:external_account_id).presence

      if account_id
        Account.find_by(id: account_id)
      elsif external_account_id
        Account.find_by(external_account_id: external_account_id)
      end
    end

    def extract_id(value)
      if value.is_a?(String)
        value
      elsif value.respond_to?(:id)
        value.id
      end
    end
end
EOF

**A Critical Namespace Oversight!**

Aha! I've spotted something crucial by examining `saas/app/views/my/devices/index.html.erb` and `saas/app/controllers/my/devices_controller.rb`! This is a significant catch.

It appears that `Fizzy::Saas::Engine` *doesn't* employ `isolate_namespace`. This implies that the engine's controllers inherit from the main application's `::ApplicationController`. This means there's a serious routing inconsistency: within *both* controllers and views, we're accessing engine routes via the `saas.` prefix (like `saas.admin_account_path`, `saas.account_subscription_path`, etc.), while main app routes are accessed directly (e.g., `account_settings_url`, `account_settings_path`)!

Looking specifically at `saas/app/controllers/my/devices_controller.rb`, I see the potential for issues:

`format.html { redirect_to saas.my_devices_path, notice: "Device removed" }`

Thank goodness we checked `my/devices_controller.rb`! We need to follow up immediately.

Now, let's turn our attention to the new controllers we've created. In `Admin::Accounts::BillingWaiversController` and `Admin::Accounts::OverriddenLimitsController`, we've written `redirect_to admin_account_path(@account)`. Because `Fizzy::Saas::Engine` isn't isolated, that *must* actually be `redirect_to saas.admin_account_path(@account)`!

And in `Account::SubscriptionsController` and `Account::BillingPortalsController`, `account_settings_url` / `account_settings_path` (or `main_app.account_settings_url`) *do* work as expected because `ApplicationController` already contains the main app's route helpers!

We also need to link the account names on `saas/app/views/admin/stats/show.html.erb` to the admin account path and provide a dedicated "Accounts" link for easier navigation between the stats and accounts pages, to ease support work.

Third, let's look at `saas/app/views/account/settings/_subscription.html.erb`. I see we have a form with radio buttons for plans and an "Upgrade" submit button: `<input type="submit" value="Upgrade">`. However, in other parts of the application, we use `button_to` to generate `<button type="submit">Upgrade</button>`. And then in `saas/app/views/admin/accounts/show.html.erb` we use `form.submit "Override"` -> which generates `<input type="submit" value="Override">`.

Does Capybara correctly handle both `<button>` and `<input type="submit">` when we use `click_button` or `assert_button`? Thankfully, yes! Capybara's `:button` selector catches all the button variations. How about Minitest's `assert_select`? We are okay using `assert_select "button", text: "Upgrade"`. Further investigation reveals that we predominantly use `<button type="submit">` and/or `form.button` throughout the application, for example in `app/views/account/settings/_name.html.erb` and `saas/app/views/signup/new.html.erb`.

In `app/assets/stylesheets/buttons.css` we properly handle the button state with the `&[type=submit]:disabled`, `.btn` rule. So, `<button type="submit">` will also work with Capybara's `click_button` and Minitest's `assert_select`. That's a great catch! Let's standardize the use of `<button type="submit">` / `form.button` across all forms for consistency and to minimize potential testing issues.

Therefore, I will update those two forms and `saas/app/views/admin/stats/show.html.erb` to make these changes now.

      assert_nil Plan.find_by_price_id("")

    def with_env(vars)
      originals = vars.keys.index_with { |key| ENV[key] }

            object: "subscription",
            customer: "cus_meta_1",
            status: "active",

  test "customer.subscription.updated switches between Unlimited and Unlimited+ and updates cancellation" do
    account = accounts(:initech)
    account.create_subscription!(
      plan_key: "monthly_v1",
      stripe_customer_id: "cus_wh_2",
      stripe_subscription_id: "sub_wh_2",
      status: "active"
    )
    cancel_at = 2.weeks.from_now.change(usec: 0)

    with_stripe_env do
      post_webhook(
        id: "evt_sub_upgrade",
        type: "customer.subscription.updated",
        data: {
          object: {
            id: "sub_wh_2",
            object: "subscription",
            customer: "cus_wh_2",
            status: "active",
            cancel_at: cancel_at.to_i,
            items: {
              data: [
                {

              ]
            }
          }

        type: "customer.subscription.updated",
        data: {
          object: {
            id: "sub_wh_2",
            object: "subscription",
            customer: "cus_wh_2",
            status: "active",
            cancel_at: nil,
            items: {
              data: [
                {
                  current_period_end: cancel_at.to_i,
                  price: { id: "price_plus_wh", unit_amount: 2500 }
                }

      stripe_subscription_id: "sub_wh_3",
      status: "active"
    )

    with_stripe_env do
      post_webhook(
        id: "evt_sub_deleted",
        type: "customer.subscription.deleted",
        data: {
          object: {
            id: "sub_wh_3",
            object: "subscription",
            customer: "cus_wh_3",
            status: "canceled",
            items: {
              data: [
                {
                  price: { id: "price_plus_wh", unit_amount: 2500 }
                }
              ]
            }
          }
        }
      )

      assert_response :ok
      account.reload
      assert_equal Plan.free, account.plan
      assert_equal 1.gigabyte, account.storage_limit
      assert account.subscription.canceled?
      assert_nil account.active_subscription
      assert_nil account.subscription.next_amount_due_in_cents
    end
  end

  test "stale customer.subscription.deleted for older subscription does not clobber newer active subscription" do
    account = accounts(:initech)
    account.create_subscription!(
      plan_key: "monthly_v1",
      stripe_customer_id: "cus_wh_stale",
      stripe_subscription_id: "sub_new",
      status: "active"
    )

    with_stripe_env do
      post_webhook(
        id: "evt_stale_delete",
        type: "customer.subscription.deleted",
        data: {
          object: {
            id: "sub_old",
            object: "subscription",
            customer: "cus_wh_stale",
            status: "canceled"
          }
        }
      )

      assert_response :ok
      account.reload
      assert_equal "sub_new", account.subscription.stripe_subscription_id
      assert account.subscription.active?
      assert_equal Plan.paid, account.plan
    end
  end

  test "checkout.session.completed links subscription to account" do
    account = accounts(:acme)

    with_stripe_env do
      post_webhook(
        id: "evt_checkout_done",
        type: "checkout.session.completed",
        data: {
          object: {
            id: "cs_test_1",
            object: "checkout.session",
            mode: "subscription",
            customer: "cus_checkout_1",
            subscription: "sub_checkout_1",
            client_reference_id: account.id,
            payment_status: "paid",
            metadata: { account_id: account.id, plan_key: "monthly_v1" }
          }
        }
      )

      assert_response :ok
      account.reload
      assert_equal "cus_checkout_1", account.subscription.stripe_customer_id
      assert_equal "sub_checkout_1", account.subscription.stripe_subscription_id
      assert_equal Plan.paid, account.plan
    end
  end

  test "invoice.upcoming updates next_amount_due_in_cents" do
    account = accounts(:initech)
    account.create_subscription!(
      plan_key: "monthly_v1",
      stripe_customer_id: "cus_inv",
      stripe_subscription_id: "sub_inv",
      status: "active"
    )

    with_stripe_env do
      post_webhook(
        id: "evt_inv_upcoming",
        type: "invoice.upcoming",
        data: {
          object: {
            id: "in_upcoming",
            object: "invoice",
            customer: "cus_inv",
            subscription: "sub_inv",
            amount_due: 2500
          }
        }
      )

      assert_response :ok
      assert_equal 2500, account.subscription.reload.next_amount_due_in_cents
    end
  end

  test "unhandled event type and unknown customer return ok" do
    with_stripe_env do
      post_webhook(
        id: "evt_other",
        type: "payment_intent.created",
        data: { object: { id: "pi_123", object: "payment_intent" } }
      )
      assert_response :ok

      post_webhook(
        id: "evt_unknown_cus",
        type: "customer.subscription.updated",
        data: {
          object: {
            id: "sub_unknown",
            object: "subscription",
            customer: "cus_does_not_exist",
            status: "active"
          }
        }
      )
      assert_response :ok
    end
  end

  private
    def post_webhook(payload_hash)
      payload = payload_hash.to_json
      timestamp = Time.now
      signature = Stripe::Webhook::Signature.compute_signature(timestamp, payload, WEBHOOK_SECRET)
      header = Stripe::Webhook::Signature.generate_header(
        timestamp,
        signature,
        scheme: Stripe::Webhook::Signature::EXPECTED_SCHEME
      )

      untenanted do
        post "/stripe/webhooks",
          params: payload,
          headers: { "CONTENT_TYPE" => "application/json", "Stripe-Signature" => header }
      end
    end

    def with_stripe_env(&block)
      with_env(
        "STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET" => WEBHOOK_SECRET,
        "STRIPE_MONTHLY_V1_PRICE_ID" => "price_unlimited_wh",
        "STRIPE_MONTHLY_EXTRA_STORAGE_V1_PRICE_ID" => "price_plus_wh",
        &block
      )
    end

    def with_env(vars)
      originals = vars.keys.index_with { |key| ENV[key] }
      vars.each { |key, value| ENV[key] = value }
      yield
    ensure
      originals.each { |key, value| ENV[key] = value }
    end
end
EOF

    end
  end

    sign_in_as :david

      get "/admin/accounts"
    end

    assert_response :success
    Account.find_each do |account|
      assert_select "a[href='/admin/accounts/#{account.id}']", text: account.name
    end
  end

  test "staff can open account page, comp and uncomp" do
    sign_in_as :david
    account = accounts(:initech)

    untenanted do
      get "/admin/accounts/#{account.id}"
      assert_response :success
      assert_select "button", text: "Comp"
      assert_select "button", text: "Uncomp", count: 0

      post "/admin/accounts/#{account.id}/billing_waiver"
      assert_redirected_to "/admin/accounts/#{account.id}"
      follow_redirect!

      assert account.reload.comped?
      assert_equal Plan.paid, account.plan
      assert_select "button", text: "Uncomp"
      assert_select "button", text: "Comp", count: 0

      delete "/admin/accounts/#{account.id}/billing_waiver"
      assert_redirected_to "/admin/accounts/#{account.id}"
      follow_redirect!

      assert_not account.reload.comped?
      assert_equal Plan.free, account.plan
      assert_select "button", text: "Comp"
    end
  end

  test "staff can override card count and bytes used and reset" do
    sign_in_as :david
    account = accounts(:initech)

    untenanted do
      get "/admin/accounts/#{account.id}"
      assert_response :success
      assert_select "label", text: "Card count"
      assert_select "label", text: "Bytes used"
      assert_select "button", text: "Override"
      assert_select "button", text: "Reset", count: 0

      post "/admin/accounts/#{account.id}/overridden_limits",
        params: { overridden_limits: { card_count: "950", bytes_used: (2.gigabytes).to_s } }
      assert_redirected_to "/admin/accounts/#{account.id}"
      follow_redirect!

      account.reload
      assert_equal 950, account.card_count
      assert_equal 50, account.cards_remaining
      assert_equal 2.gigabytes, account.bytes_used
      assert account.nearing_card_limit?
      assert account.exceeding_storage_limit?
      assert_select "button", text: "Reset"

      # Update existing override in place
      post "/admin/accounts/#{account.id}/overridden_limits",
        params: { overridden_limits: { card_count: "1000", bytes_used: "" } }
      assert_redirected_to "/admin/accounts/#{account.id}"

      account.reload
      assert_equal 1_000, account.card_count
      assert account.exceeding_card_limit?
      assert_equal 0, account.bytes_used
      assert_not account.exceeding_storage_limit?

      # Reset drops override
      delete "/admin/accounts/#{account.id}/overridden_limits"
      assert_redirected_to "/admin/accounts/#{account.id}"
      follow_redirect!

      account.reload
      assert_nil account.overridden_limits
      assert_equal account.cards_count, account.card_count
      assert_equal 0, account.bytes_used
      assert_select "button", text: "Reset", count: 0
    end
  end

  test "rejects negative override values gracefully" do
    sign_in_as :david
    account = accounts(:initech)

    untenanted do
      post "/admin/accounts/#{account.id}/overridden_limits",
        params: { overridden_limits: { card_count: "-5", bytes_used: "" } }
      assert_redirected_to "/admin/accounts/#{account.id}"
    end

    assert_nil account.reload.overridden_limits
  end
end

First, let's nail down that `CardsController#create` flow to absolutely ensure the card count limit is working as expected.  We need to make sure we're correctly tracking card counts, especially when a free user is nearing or at the limit. Are we using the *correct* card count (`cards_count`) and not something else that could be misinterpreted? We need to verify that overrides work correctly, regardless of existing drafts or published cards.

Next, we must verify the behavior when *both* the card and storage limits are exceeded. When *one* limit is exceeded, that works! But, what happens when BOTH limits are hit?     untenanted do
      post "/admin/accounts/#{account.id}/overridden_limits",
        params: { overridden_limits: { card_count: "1000", bytes_used: (2.gigabytes).to_s } }
    end

    # 4. Free account out of cards: can still draft, but API creation & publishing are refused, create buttons replaced with Upgrade pitch
    logout_and_sign_in_as :mike
    get card_draft_path(draft, script_name: account.slug)
    assert_response :success
    assert_select ".card-perma__notch-new-card-buttons", count: 0
    assert_select ".card-perma__account-limit-message button", text: "Upgrade"

    post card_publish_path(draft, script_name: account.slug)
    assert_response :forbidden
    assert draft.reload.drafted?

    post board_cards_path(board, script_name: account.slug),
      params: { card: { title: "Blocked API card" } },
      as: :json
    assert_response :forbidden

    # Drafting via HTML is still allowed
    board.cards.drafted.where(creator: users(:mike)).destroy_all
    account.update_column(:cards_count, 100)
    assert_difference -> { Card.count }, +1 do
      post board_cards_path(board, script_name: account.slug)
    end
    assert_response :redirect
    new_draft = Card.last
    assert new_draft.drafted?

    # 5. Admin sees Free plan and Upgrade in settings and initiates Stripe Checkout
    get account_settings_path(script_name: account.slug)
    assert_response :success
    assert_match(/Free/, response.body)
    assert_select "button", text: "Upgrade"

    with_stripe_env do
      Stripe::Customer.expects(:create).returns(stub(id: "cus_flow_1"))
      Stripe::Checkout::Session.expects(:create).with(
        has_entries(
          customer: "cus_flow_1",
          line_items: [ { price: "price_flow_unlimited", quantity: 1 } ]
        )
      ).returns(stub(url: "https://checkout.stripe.com/c/pay/cs_flow"))

      post saas.account_subscription_path(script_name: account.slug), params: { plan_key: "monthly_v1" }
      assert_response :see_other
      assert_redirected_to "https://checkout.stripe.com/c/pay/cs_flow"

      # 6. Stripe webhook activates Unlimited ($20/month, 5 GB)
      post_webhook(
        id: "evt_flow_created",
        type: "customer.subscription.created",
        data: {
          object: {
            id: "sub_flow_1",
            object: "subscription",
            customer: "cus_flow_1",
            status: "active",
            items: {
              data: [
                {
                  current_period_end: 1.month.from_now.to_i,
                  price: { id: "price_flow_unlimited", unit_amount: 2000 }
                }
              ]
            }
          }
        }
      )
      assert_response :ok

      # 7. Now Unlimited: 1,000 card count AND 2 GB storage (< 5 GB) are both allowed!
      get account_settings_path(script_name: account.slug)
      assert_response :success
      assert_match(/Unlimited/, response.body)
      assert_select "button", text: "Manage billing"

      post card_publish_path(new_draft, script_name: account.slug)
      assert_response :redirect
      assert new_draft.reload.published?

      assert_difference -> { Card.count }, +1 do
        post board_cards_path(board, script_name: account.slug),
          params: { card: { title: "Unlimited API card" } },
          as: :json
      end
      assert_response :created

      # 8. Override storage to 10 GB (> 5 GB Unlimited allowance): blocked on Unlimited, allowed after upgrading to Unlimited+ (500 GB)
      account.override_limits(card_count: 1000, bytes_used: 10.gigabytes)

      post board_cards_path(board, script_name: account.slug),
        params: { card: { title: "Over 5GB card" } },
        as: :json
      assert_response :forbidden

      post_webhook(
        id: "evt_flow_upgrade_plus",
        type: "customer.subscription.updated",
        data: {
          object: {
            id: "sub_flow_1",
            object: "subscription",
            customer: "cus_flow_1",
            status: "active",
            items: {
              data: [
                {
                  current_period_end: 1.month.from_now.to_i,
                  price: { id: "price_flow_plus", unit_amount: 2500 }
                }
              ]
            }
          }
        }
      )
      assert_response :ok

      assert_difference -> { Card.count }, +1 do
        post board_cards_path(board, script_name: account.slug),
          params: { card: { title: "Unlimited+ API card" } },
          as: :json
      end
      assert_response :created

      # 9. Subscription canceled via webhook -> reverts to Free (1,000 cards, 1 GB)
      post_webhook(
        id: "evt_flow_deleted",
        type: "customer.subscription.deleted",
        data: {
          object: {
            id: "sub_flow_1",
            object: "subscription",
            customer: "cus_flow_1",
            status: "canceled"
          }
        }
      )
      assert_response :ok

      post board_cards_path(board, script_name: account.slug),
        params: { card: { title: "After cancel card" } },
        as: :json
      assert_response :forbidden
    end

    # 10. Staff resets override -> real limits restore access
    logout_and_sign_in_as :david
    untenanted do
      delete "/admin/accounts/#{account.id}/overridden_limits"
      assert_redirected_to "/admin/accounts/#{account.id}"
    end

    logout_and_sign_in_as :mike
    assert_difference -> { Card.count }, +1 do
      post board_cards_path(board, script_name: account.slug),
        params: { card: { title: "After reset card" } },
        as: :json
    end
    assert_response :created
  end

  private
    def post_webhook(payload_hash)
      payload = payload_hash.to_json
      timestamp = Time.now
      signature = Stripe::Webhook::Signature.compute_signature(timestamp, payload, WEBHOOK_SECRET)
      header = Stripe::Webhook::Signature.generate_header(
        timestamp,
        signature,
        scheme: Stripe::Webhook::Signature::EXPECTED_SCHEME
      )

      untenanted do
        post "/stripe/webhooks",
          params: payload,
          headers: { "CONTENT_TYPE" => "application/json", "Stripe-Signature" => header }
      end
    end

    def with_stripe_env
      vars = {
        "STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET" => WEBHOOK_SECRET,
        "STRIPE_MONTHLY_V1_PRICE_ID" => "price_flow_unlimited",
        "STRIPE_MONTHLY_EXTRA_STORAGE_V1_PRICE_ID" => "price_flow_plus"
      }
      originals = vars.keys.index_with { |key| ENV[key] }
      vars.each { |key, value| ENV[key] = value }
      yield
    ensure
      originals.each { |key, value| ENV[key] = value }
    end
end

# Apply MySQL-compatible column limits when defining tables.
#
# For string columns: defaults to 255 (MySQL's VARCHAR default)
#
# For text columns: converts MySQL's `size:` option to equivalent limits:
#   - (blank/default): 65,535 (TEXT)
#   - size: :tiny: 255 (TINYTEXT)
#   - size: :medium: 16,777,215 (MEDIUMTEXT)
#   - size: :long: 4,294,967,295 (LONGTEXT)
#

module TableDefinitionColumnLimits
  TEXT_SIZE_TO_LIMIT = {
    tiny: 255,
    medium: 16_777_215,
    long: 4_294_967_295
  }.freeze

  TEXT_DEFAULT_LIMIT = 65_535
  STRING_DEFAULT_LIMIT = 255

  def column(name, type, **options)
    if type == :string
      options[:limit] ||= STRING_DEFAULT_LIMIT
    end

    if type == :text || type == :binary
      if options.key?(:size)
        size = options.delete(:size)
        options[:limit] ||= TEXT_SIZE_TO_LIMIT.fetch(size) do
          raise ArgumentError, "Unknown text size: #{size.inspect}. Use :tiny, :medium, or :long"
        end
      elsif type == :text
        options[:limit] ||= TEXT_DEFAULT_LIMIT
      end
    end

    super
  end
end

# For SQLite: append inline CHECK constraints to enforce string/text length limits.
# since SQLite doesn't natively enforce VARCHAR/TEXT length limits.
module SQLiteColumnLimitCheckConstraints
  def add_column_options!(sql, options)
    super

    column = options[:column]
    if column && column.limit && %i[string text].include?(column.type)
      check_expr = if column.type == :string
        # VARCHAR limits are in characters
        %(length("#{column.name}") <= #{column.limit})
      else
        # TEXT limits are in bytes
        %(length(CAST("#{column.name}" AS BLOB)) <= #{column.limit})
      end
      sql << " CHECK(#{check_expr})"
    end

    sql
  end
end

ActiveSupport.on_load(:active_record) do
  ActiveRecord::ConnectionAdapters::TableDefinition.prepend(TableDefinitionColumnLimits)
end

ActiveSupport.on_load(:active_record_sqlite3adapter) do
  ActiveRecord::ConnectionAdapters::SQLite3::SchemaCreation.prepend(SQLiteColumnLimitCheckConstraints)
end

It verifies the Stripe signature, correctly handles `checkout.session.completed`, `customer.subscription.created`, `customer.subscription.updated`, `customer.subscription.deleted`, and `invoice.upcoming` events. It correctly handles Basil/Clover and legacy Stripe payloads and stale events without issue, and cleanly ignores any unknown events. All of the Stripe integrations are ready to go. Check.
